summary:
The story across every rating right now is the SP category meltdown — all four models sit on identical 9-game losing streaks, cratering to 36% (8-14, n=22) over the last 14 days against season marks near 53-55%. That's a uniform -16 to -18pt collapse, and it's not noise given the sample consistency across R1-R4. Meanwhile bullpen and hitting are carrying the slate: bullpen is hot for every rating (64%, 14-8, n=22, +11.6pts for R1-R3), and hitting is the standout, with R2 running 68% (15-7, n=22, +18.9pts) and R4 matching that 68% clip too. Bullpen_fatigue chips in a steady +8-9pt lift across the board. Trust the glove and the lineup reads today, not the starter grades.

Both games on the slate are consensus plays across all four ratings, which is rare and worth leaning into. MIL @ LAD shows the strongest average delta of the day — R2 the most confident at -2.02 on Milwaukee — and MIL has been a license to print this season at 46-22 (68%, n=68) with a 26-12, +17.0u strong-play record. That's the best team-volume profile on the board, and the fact that it's a road SP matchup against Glasnow actually plays into today's theme: don't let the SP read scare you off, since the model's edge here is coming from the same bullpen/hitting signals that are running hot, not from starter grades. The TBR @ CLE lean is milder (R1 +1.44 down to R4 +0.77 on Cleveland), a softer consensus where the delta shrinks sharply from R1 to R4 — worth smaller sizing. TBR's own team-when-liked number (69%, 42-19, n=61, strong 26-11 +21.0u) argues for caution fading them, but the rating consensus still favors Cleveland, so this is the day's more marginal, lower-conviction side. With trends+sp still the best-performing category pair historically (57.6%, n=632) despite SP's current cold streak, don't abandon SP combos entirely — just don't bet SP in isolation while it's 9 losses deep.
